name: DX11.1 Forced Sample Count Optimization

# DX11.1 Forced Sample Count Optimization
Also called: Forced Sample Count MSAA Voxelization
## Overview
This method leverages the DirectX 11.1 "Forced Sample Count" feature to perform MSAA rasterization without binding an MSAA render target [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. It serves as a memory-efficient alternative to standard [MSAA voxelization](#7412-msaa-voxelization.md) by reducing video memory (vidmem) overhead [S2, unofficial].
## How it works
**Inputs and Outputs:** Not given in the sources. [G]
**Data Structures:** Not given in the sources. [G]
**Steps:**
1. Configure the rasterizer state to enable the Forced Sample Count feature in DirectX 11.1, which activates MSAA rasterization without requiring an MSAA render target to be bound [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].
**Formulas:** Not given in the sources. [G]
**Parameters:** Typical sample count values are not given in the sources. [G]
**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:** The method is relatively aggressive and does not provide genuine [conservative rasterization](#2936-conservative-rasterization.md) [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. Primitives that lie between subsamples may fail to be voxelized properly, creating "holes" in the resulting grid [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. These gaps are avoidable by ensuring the voxel grid resolution is sufficiently fine relative to the sizes of the voxelized primitives [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].
## Operating characteristics
*   **Memory:** Reduces vidmem cost compared to standard MSAA voxelization, which requires binding an MSAA render target [S2, unofficial].

This technique was discussed in the context of [GPU voxelization](#2633-gpu-voxelization.md) fundamentals [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. It was presented as a practical optimization for DirectX 11.1 hardware, allowing developers to utilize MSAA coverage benefits without the associated memory penalty [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].
